summary: Curtailment of reserved-pool throughput traced to interleaved tenant heartbeats and transient GPU scarcity
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-12 05:10 UTC BrightLedger is reporting stepwise drops in throughput (p50 -> p99 token throughput) for routes pinned to their dedicated pool. Impact: customer seeing 30-60% throughput loss for 30-90s windows; increased latency and queue growth causing degraded SLAs for their production pipelines. Environment: BrightLedger dedicated pool in prod-us-west, reserved cluster id rc-77b9. Observed behavior: periodic ~45s windows where new requests queue despite GPUs showing nominal utilization in cluster telemetry. Autoscaler logs show rapid shrink/grow events coincident with the windows. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send steady generation traffic using their traffic pattern (many short streams + occasional 4k token bursts). 2) Observe queue growth and throughput steps in 1-3 minute periods. 3) Correlate with scheduler heartbeats and eviction traces. Expected behavior: smooth throughput with autoscaler holding capacity steady for pinned reserved pool. Frequency: recurring daily during BrightLedger's morning ingest window (04:50–06:30 UTC).
comments: 2026-03-12 06:00 - Support (Maya Chen): Initial triage. Customer reported throughput drops starting 05:10 UTC. Collected request IDs and sample traces. Requested permission to access cluster logs and take core dumps if needed.

2026-03-12 07:15 - SRE (Diego Ramirez): Confirmed queue growth on rc-77b9. Noticed autoscaler shrink at 05:12 then immediate grow at 05:13. Suspect eviction window aligned with heartbeat jitter. Asking infra for low-level GPU attach/detach events.

2026-03-12 09:02 - Customer (BrightLedger - Jenna Park): We observed 10% request timeout rate during window, unable to re-route due to pinned model. Provided additional logs and example request-ids SUP-BRIGHT-0001..0006.

2026-03-13 10:30 - SRE (Carlos Ortega): Ran kernel-level telemetry. Found brief NVLink retransmit spikes and pci_error_count bump on two nodes at 05:12. Possibly causing device detach which triggers scheduler eviction heuristics. Recommending temporarily pinning to alternate nodes while investigation continues.

2026-03-14 11:00 - Support (Maya Chen): Notified customer of temporary mitigation: apply node-affinity override to avoid nodes with nvlink/pci jitter. Customer accepted and applied during a test window; they saw throughput restoration in the test run.
2026-03-14 12:30 - PM (Rina Sato): Added to follow-up action list for a longer term autoscaler/heartbeat hardening plan. Linking to INT-1180 for infra remediation tracking.
investigation_notes: Summary of findings: 1) Autoscaler shrink/expand cycles line up with bursty short-stream patterns from the customer combined with intermittent PCI/NVLink retransmit spikes on two GPUs in the reserved cluster. 2) Scheduler heartbeat jitter (30-70ms spikes) caused the node-health evaluator to flag GPUs as transiently unavailable, triggering early eviction of some batch slots. 3) Eviction + immediate subsequent autoscaler grow created a short window where incoming short-streams serialized onto fewer slots, causing step-function throughput loss. Evidence: - autoscaler logs (shrink at 05:12:03 UTC, grow at 05:12:50 UTC) - scheduler heartbeat trace (node rc-77b9-node-12: heartbeat latency spikes 35ms->120ms) - dmesg/pci logs: pcie_error_count increment + nvlink retransmit counters on node-12 and node-15 - serving runtime traces show batcher backlog spike and slot steal events during same window Hypotheses considered: noisy-tenant sidecar causing PCI noise (rejected: no sidecars with IO heavy tasks found), thermal throttling (rejected: temps steady), ephemeral training/job landing on infra plane (partial: found short-lived eviction from background orchestration for scheduled maintenance on node-15). Actions taken: - Reproduced behavior in controlled replay using customer's short-stream pattern. - Temporarily blacklisted node-12 and node-15 for BrightLedger pool; observed restored throughput in replay. - Grabbed core traces and uploaded to S3 (s3://redwood-support/SUP-720489/cores/). Next diagnostics: correlate NVLink firmware logs with cloud provider host telemetry and schedule maintenance windows with infra ops.
resolution: Temporary workaround: Blacklisted two problematic nodes from BrightLedger's reserved pool (node-12, node-15) and applied an autoscaler guard to avoid shrinking below the pool commit during high-frequency short-stream windows. Customer confirmed improved throughput in a controlled test (03/14 test window). Long-term fix plan: 1) Infra to investigate and remediate NVLink/PCI jitter on the two nodes (INT-1180 opened). 2) Implement scheduler heartbeat smoothing and add a short grace period before triggering evictions when heartbeat jitter is detected. 3) Autoscaler change: add workload-shape awareness so short-stream dominated workloads do not cause premature shrink. Rollout notes: - Temporary guard rolled out to affected cluster 2026-03-14 09:20 UTC. - Infra remediation planned for 2026-03-16 maintenance window (coordinating with cloud provider). - Follow-up: run a 72-hour post-fix soak and capture detailed batcher histograms. Follow-ups/Docs: add a runbook entry "dedicated: handle transient-device-jitter" to Confluence and surface pattern to Customer Success for proactive outreach to other heavy short-stream customers.
notes: Customer impact prioritized due to P1 SLA. No data exfiltration or security issues detected. Billing unaffected.
